_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Apollo Hospitals (consolidated, Rs crore). Built by reported business: Healthcare Services (hospitals), Apollo HealthCo (pharmacy distribution + Apollo 24/7) and AHLL; group EBITDA = sum of the three (post-Ind AS 116, as reported). The hospital revenue path comes from a bed build (beds x occupancy / ALOS x revenue per in-patient) kept in `businessLines` and checked against model revenue in APOLLOHOSP.ctx.js. Profit is attributable to owners (APOLLOHOSP.patch.js); the tax line carries tax plus minorities. Screener 'borrowings' include lease liabilities and Advent's CCPS in Apollo HealthCo, so the model's net cash is net of both; the SOTP adds the CCPS back (Advent's claim sits in the 40.4% of NewCo not owned by Apollo's shareholders). Valued on sum of the parts, as the street does.

segments.name: Healthcare Services (hospitals)
segments._why: From the bed build in businessLines.hcs: average operating beds 8,600 / 9,250 / 9,550 (Jun-26: 8,352; +620 commissioned beds over 12-18 months, Gurgaon 380 census beds from Oct-2026, 327 brownfield beds in FY28-29), occupancy 69% / 69.5% / 70.5% (Q1FY27 70%, established 72%; new beds dilute), ALOS 3.10 / 3.05 / 3.02 days, revenue per in-patient +7.6% / +7.0% / +6.5% (~5% price + case mix; +8% in Q1FY27). FY27 +19.5% sits inside management's 18-20%; FY28 +17.8% (guidance: 13-14% established + ~7% new over 24 months); FY29 +12.7% as few beds open before the FY30-31 greenfields.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 24.4%, Q1FY27 24.2% (established 25.9%, new hospitals -Rs38 cr). FY27 23.8%: established ~26% on ~Rs14,250 cr less ~Rs175 cr of new-hospital losses (guided ~Rs150 cr, rising ~Rs20 cr a quarter with Gurgaon). FY28 24.1%: new cluster breaks even by Q3-Q4 FY28. FY29 24.7%: established inching up (management), new units profitable, early pre-opening costs for the FY30-31 greenfields.

segments.name: Apollo HealthCo (pharmacy distribution + 24/7)
segments._why: FY26 +19%, Q1FY27 +20% (+22% excluding an exited corporate partner); offline distribution +22%, digital pharmacy and diagnostics +25-30%. 19% / 17% / 16%: store additions (~7,440 stores) and private label, slowing as the base grows.
segments._marginWhy: EBITDA after the 24/7 operating cost and ESOP charge (reported basis): FY25 1.8%, FY26 4.5%, Q1FY27 5.8%. Before digital costs the margin is ~8.8%; 24/7 costs ~Rs80 cr a quarter (guided steady), ESOP ~Rs40 cr in FY27. 6.0% / 6.8% / 7.2% assumes digital breakeven in FY27 and pre-digital margin of 8.9-9.1%, below the ~6.5-7% guided for the combined NewCo exit run-rate once Keimed's ~3% margin is blended in, i.e. we assume slower margin gains than management.

segments.name: AHLL (clinics, diagnostics, specialty care)
segments._why: Apollo Cradle and Fertility (Rs450 cr revenue in FY26) leave for Cloudnine; CCI approved on 1-Sep-2026 and management expected completion in Q2FY27, so we deconsolidate from Q3FY27. Continuing AHLL (~Rs1,415 cr in FY26) grows ~18% a year (diagnostics +31% in Q1FY27, primary care +12%): FY27 Rs1,889 cr (+1%, half a year of Cradle), FY28 Rs1,968 cr (+4%), FY29 +17%.
segments._marginWhy: FY26 11.4% (incl. Cradle/Fertility, ~Rs45 cr IGAAP EBITDA); Q1FY27 11.8%. Diagnostics margin 14% in Q1FY27, targeted ~20% within 6-8 quarters. 12.2% / 13.5% / 14.5%.

_unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any segment
_unallocWhy: Segments sum to consolidated EBITDA as reported (FY26 Rs3,769 cr; Screener shows Rs3,779 cr after a Rs10 cr reclassification).

businessLines._why: Hospital revenue build (network KPIs include the 22%-owned Delhi hospital, as the company reports them). discharges = average operating beds x occupancy x 365 / ALOS; in-patient revenue = discharges x average revenue per in-patient (ARPP); network net revenue = in-patient revenue / in-patient share (81.7% in FY26: 628,998 x Rs178,434 = Rs11,224 cr of Rs13,740 cr); consolidated hospital revenue = network revenue x 91.4% (FY26 Rs12,555 cr of Rs13,740 cr; Q1FY27 91.7%), removing Delhi. Average beds 8,600 / 9,250 / 9,550 (FY26 average ~8,070; Jun-26 8,352); FY26 calibrates to 67.7% occupancy on average beds (reported 67%).

_capexWhy: Cash capex ~Rs2,200 / 2,200 / 2,300 cr plus new leases (right-of-use additions, Rs203 cr in FY26 and Rs522 cr in FY25) ~Rs250 cr a year, because the model's net debt includes lease liabilities. Cash capex = ~Rs550 cr recurring hospital capex (management) + ~Rs1,500 cr a year of the Rs7,500 cr still to be spent on the FY31 bed plan + ~Rs150 cr for HealthCo and AHLL. FY26 capex Rs1,962 cr (Screener).
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs876 cr (incl. right-of-use) = 5.1% of average gross block (Rs17,220 cr); Q1FY27 Rs235 cr (Rs940 cr annualised). 5.0% gives FY27E ~Rs975 cr with Gurgaon opening; the engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
_treasuryWhy: Zero because the engine would apply it to net cash after lease liabilities and CCPS, which is negative. Treasury income is built on gross treasury in `otherIncome`.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 note 32 and note 10 (Screener's other income also carries the share of associates). (1) Treasury income: FY26 Rs139 cr (bank deposits Rs53.7 cr + mutual-fund fair-value gains Rs62.5 cr + gains on financial assets Rs22.8 cr) on ~Rs2,600 cr average treasury = ~5.3%. We take 5.5% on opening company treasury of Rs2,336 / 2,350 / 2,300 cr (capex absorbs free cash; ~Rs750 cr of Cloudnine cash arrives in FY27) = Rs128 / 129 / 127 cr. (2) Recurring other items: interest on other financial assets Rs20.3 cr, dividends Rs2.7 cr, miscellaneous Rs26.7 cr, write-backs Rs1.0 cr = ~Rs45-50 cr. (3) Share of associates (Delhi hospital, FHPL and others): Rs44.9 cr in FY26, Rs13.4 cr in Q1FY27 -> Rs52 / 58 / 64 cr. Total Rs225 / 235 / 240 cr vs FY26 Rs236.5 cr like-for-like (Screener Rs207 cr after the Rs19 cr labour-code exceptional and a Rs10 cr reclassification) and Rs231 cr in the twelve months to Jun-26. One-offs left out: PPE disposal gain Rs1.9 cr.

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits over 12 months inside other financial assets (Rs174 cr non-current + Rs28 cr current, AR FY26 note 14), not in Screener's cash or investments; with them Screener cash (Rs1,117 cr) and mutual funds (Rs1,017 cr) give the company's Rs2,336 cr of cash and treasury.

_interestLabel: Finance cost (bank debt, lease interest, CCPS)
_interestWhy: FY26 Rs450 cr (lease interest Rs174 cr); Q1FY27 Rs120 cr (Rs482 cr annualised). Gross bank debt Rs3,244 cr and leases Rs2,877 cr at Jun-26; new leases and capex funding add ~Rs25 cr a year.
_taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). FY26: PBT Rs2,661 cr, tax Rs658 cr (24.7%), minorities Rs61 cr, attributable PAT Rs1,942 cr = 27.0% leakage. Q1FY27: PBT Rs799 cr, tax Rs188 cr (23.6%), minorities Rs30 cr = 27.3%. We take 24.5% tax + ~3.2% minorities (Assam, Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Imperial and others; Rs110-130 cr a year).
_payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs20 a share (Rs288 cr) = 15% of EPS; capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: Net debt incl. leases but excl. CCPS is ~Rs3,600 cr, ~3% of enterprise value, so WACC is close to the 11.6% cost of equity the engine uses (beta 0.85: defensive demand, but regulatory and execution risk).
dcf._tgWhy: Healthcare spending grows faster than nominal GDP as insurance spreads; 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~15% to 9% by year 15 as the bed plan completes and pharmacy matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 17.5% consolidated: hospitals ~25% and pharmacy ~7.5% at a roughly even revenue mix, plus AHLL.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from ~6.5% of revenue to 5.5% (replacement ~3.8% plus growth beds); FY26 7.8%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Gurgaon and the new hospitals fill a year early, price increases stick (no regulatory caps), established margins move to 27%, HealthCo hits the guided 7% NewCo margin in FY28 and NewCo lists at pharmacy-retail multiples.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The Parliamentary panel's pricing ideas turn into room-rent and package caps, new hospitals in the North and West ramp slowly, digital losses persist, and the market pays mid-cycle multiples for hospitals and a distribution multiple for NewCo.

parts.name: Hospitals (Healthcare Services)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Post-Ind AS EBITDA; lease liabilities are in the net debt line. Multiple derived in the valuation chapter.

parts.name: Apollo HealthCo: 59.6% of NewCo
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E EBITDA after 24/7 cost × NewCo multiple × 59.6%
parts.note: NewCo EV/EBITDA 18x (bull 24x, bear 13x) × 59.6% look-through for Apollo's shareholders (42.1% direct + 15% held by Apollo + ~2.5% through FHPL).

parts.name: Keimed: 59.6% of its value in NewCo
parts.metricLabel: GAM Sep-28E Keimed EBITDA ~Rs705 cr × NewCo multiple × 59.6%
parts.note: Keimed is not consolidated today; it merges into NewCo under the scheme. Q1FY27 EBITDA Rs134 cr (3.2% margin); we grow it ~15% a year.

parts.name: AHLL (continuing: clinics, diagnostics, Spectra, dialysis)
parts.note: Multiple derived from listed diagnostics peers, discounted for lower margins.

parts.name: Cloudnine deal: ~Rs750 cr cash + 9.9% stake at deal value less 20%
parts.note: Cradle and Fertility sold at ~Rs1,550 cr (~35x EBITDA); bull 10%, bear 30% discount on the stake.

parts.name: Delhi hospital (IMCL, 22.03%) at market less 20%, replacing book
parts.metricLabel: 2.02 cr shares × Rs348.95 (30-Sep-2026) × 0.8 − Rs179 cr book in model cash

parts.name: Add back: Advent CCPS (in model debt; Advent's claim is in NewCo's 40.4%)
parts.metricLabel: CCPS carrying value, Mar-26 (AR FY26 note 22)
parts.note: Converts into NewCo equity when the scheme takes effect; counting it as debt and also taking only 59.6% of NewCo would deduct Advent twice.

parts.name: Less: Keimed shares and FHPL held in model cash (inside the 59.6%)
parts.metricLabel: Keimed Rs800 cr at fair value + FHPL Rs60 cr at book (Mar-26)
parts.note: Both become part of NewCo's share register; already valued through the 59.6%.

parts.name: Add back: 40.4% of HealthCo net debt (NewCo-level debt shared with Advent and Keimed owners)
parts.note: Keimed's own net debt is not disclosed and is not deducted (see gaps).

parts.name: Less: minorities in hospital subsidiaries (3.41% of hospital equity value)
parts.metricLabel: 3.41% (FY26 hospital minorities Rs57.4 cr ÷ hospital PAT before minorities Rs1,685 cr) × (hospital EV − ~Rs3,100 cr hospital net debt incl. leases)
parts.note: Assam 23.8%, Lucknow 49%, Ahmedabad 50%, Imperial 10%, Indore 45%, Nellore 19%, Lavasa 49%, Kerala 40% (AR FY26 note 21). Equivalent to ~Rs86 cr of Sep-28E minority profit × 42.5x (= 24x × 0.972 ÷ 0.549 PAT/EBITDA). Bull/bear use each case's hospital EBITDA and multiple.

parts.name: Less: minorities in AHLL step-down subsidiaries
parts.metricLabel: FY26 AHLL-line minorities Rs5.7 cr × AHLL multiple ÷ 0.549 (same PAT/EBITDA conversion)
parts.note: AHLL itself is 100% owned since Mar-2026; the remaining minority sits in step-down subsidiaries (AR FY26 note 21). HealthCo minorities (Rs1.1 cr) are not deducted: NewCo is already valued at Apollo's 59.6%.

parts.name: Net debt at Sep-28E (model: borrowings incl. leases and CCPS less cash and investments)
parts.note: Mar-26: Screener borrowings Rs8,493 cr (bank debt Rs3,202 cr + CCPS Rs2,457 cr + leases Rs2,834 cr) less cash Rs1,117 cr, investments Rs2,179 cr and deposits Rs202 cr.

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street values Apollo (Prabhudas Lilladher, Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities, Antique): hospitals on EV/EBITDA, the pharmacy and digital business on its own multiple and Apollo's 59.6% share of NewCo, AHLL separately, less net debt.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on consolidated earnings: own forward P/E median (forwardMedian) adjusted for the sector de-rating.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF on consolidated cash flows, 11.6% discount rate, 6% terminal growth.
